of responsibility, in the presence of fate to be free from the
power of fate, and so free from the stresses of fear. When we
have this faith, then God is present for us not only in nature
but in the world and life as a whole, in history as a whole
with its heights and depths, in the humdrum world of every
day as well as in the relaxation of festival days. The conse-
quence is that the presence of God in nature takes on for us a
new meaning. What is that?
1. He who has this faith understands the presence of God
in nature as the invitation of the God who is calling man
unto Himself, who is driving man to seek Himself. In this
light he understands too that nature-piety of which we have
been speaking. He understands it as a flight to God, which is
not aware of its own true nature and meaning. For if nature-
piety is genuine and true, it is a witness to the sin which is the
controlling factor in human history and the life of responsi-
bility and anxiety. As an escape from the humdrum world
of everyday life and work, it bears witness to the fact that
this life is empty of God, that God is not felt to be expressed
within it. But precisely as such a flight, nature-piety attests
also that man is driven on every side to seek God and is
impelled by the yearning to attain the presence of God,
which embraces man with sustaining and liberating power.
2. The Christian believer rejoices in the presence of God
in nature; the word which calls him to believe causes him
also to be certain of the nearness of God in nature, and to
receive with thankfulness and praise all the manifold gifts
of nature as the gifts of God. And again, the divine in nature
constantly leads him back to the divine presence which
speaks out in the Word; for he does not defy nature, he sees
that in spite of all her gifts she remains ambiguous for man;
it is the hidden God who is present in her.
3. The Christian believer who is assured of God's presence
in nature, even though he cannot contemplate the truth of
God in nature, praises God for His presence therein—a
presence which is both bestowing and questioning. And
